set.approach: Park just past the seasonal gate, at the same spot used for Little Free Library, and head west to the formation. The slab faces away from the direction you approach and is easy to miss until you are on it. The route is right of center, left of an arete.

Park at the dam at Lundy Lake and follow the trail that climbs the lake's south shore toward Oneida Lake. The route is on the final prominent buttress on the drainage's right-hand side, reached by talus from the trail; the low-angle upper arete is a key marker. It begins in an alcove with some third- and fourth-class climbing, then two bolts on easy ground gain a pedestal.

review.notes: Area page and route page ("rap the route").

set.approach: Park at the Lundy dam and follow the trail toward Oneida Lake. The climb is on the right-hand skyline, the final big feature before the lake, and begins a short way left of Electric Lundy Land.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route, tying knots in the rope ends, or walk off.

set.approach: From the small dirt pull-in beneath the face, hike north to a subtle ridge that rises west toward the bluff, to a very large black oak, which marks where to traverse left through the woods and around to the base. The old trail has been reclaimed by the forest. The route lies between Innervision and Whippersnapper.

review.notes: Area page and route page. Pitch count 3 matches the page.

set.approach: Start from the Pine Creek pack station and hike the Pine Creek Pass trail uphill. Pipe Wall lies directly beside the path and is the first of the Brownstone walls you come to. The route starts on the two slab bolts at the toe of the wall, shared with Pipe Dream, and goes straight up the headwall.

Start from the Pine Creek pack station and hike the Pine Creek Pass trail uphill. Pipe Wall lies directly beside the path and is the first of the Brownstone walls you come to. It is the leftmost line on the wall, marked by two bolts on a slab at its foot.

Start from the Pine Creek pack station and hike the Pine Creek Pass trail uphill. Pipe Wall lies directly beside the path and is the first of the Brownstone walls you come to. The route starts at the foot of the wall, a step from the trail.
set.descent_text: Lower from the top, tying a knot in the rope end and swinging right on the way down.

set.approach: From the Children's Forest car park, walk west on the paved road, past the gate into Shady Cove campground, and drop through the campsite to a trail leaving its northwest corner. Follow the trail north and then west under a power line. Preschool Rock is the first cliff you see, with its climbs on the east face. The route is on the arete right of Love Child.

Hike up to the Church Domes; the Rectory south face is the usual way in to this wall. It begins on the steep, tall part of the wall near its middle, left of the giant horizontal bands, between a tall flake and a small pine.

review.notes: Area pages and route page ("equipped to lower off").

set.approach: Hike up to the Church Domes and to the Rectory. The route is on the west face, right of Going My Way, up obvious bolts.

Park in the small dirt turnout beside Highway 38 and go straight uphill; the approach is short but steep. Be careful not to knock rocks onto the road. The route is on the right side of the west face and climbs a steep arete before stepping left onto the face.

From the Lake George parking area take the Crystal Lake trail, turn left at the sign to the lake, go around it and take the climbers trail on the left. Continue past the Kilt Wall to Schoolboy Buttress. The route is the arete at the very left side of the buttress, as you come up and around into an alcove.

From the Lake George parking area take the Crystal Lake trail, turn left at the sign to the lake, go around it and take the climbers trail on the left. Continue past the Kilt Wall to Schoolboy Buttress. The route takes a rounded arete whose first three bolts are in the dish beside it; two harder routes lie to the left and a gear route in a prominent dihedral lies to the right.

From the Lake George parking area take the Crystal Lake trail, turn left at the sign to the lake, go around it and take the climbers trail on the left. Continue past the Kilt Wall to Schoolboy Buttress. It is the next-to-last line at the far left end of the buttress and climbs a chimney with a roof over it.

From the Lake George parking area take the Crystal Lake trail, turn left at the sign to the lake, go around it and take the climbers trail on the left. Continue past the Kilt Wall to Schoolboy Buttress. The route is just right of Made in the Shade.

From the north shore of Big Bear Lake, park where Greenway Drive meets Pioneer Lane and take the trails that wander up the hillside; the formations sit on the south-facing slope above. Secret Spot Rock is hidden in the trees, a hike directly uphill from Shark Fin. The route is on the right side of the south face, just right of Mr. Friction, and starts from a block on the right.

From the north shore of Big Bear Lake, park where Greenway Drive meets Pioneer Lane and take the trails that wander up the hillside; the formations sit on the south-facing slope above. Secret Spot Rock is hidden in the trees, a hike directly uphill from Shark Fin. The route is in the center of the south face, just right of Dirty Little Secret; start up that route and then move right.

Park at Lake George and hike up the climbers trail to Dike Wall, then keep walking beyond the established north face routes. Sector Mellow is the obvious slab reached first; Sector Evil Seed is a scramble up and around the right side of it. This is the right-hand route on the Sector Mellow wall.

This is the left-hand route on the Sector Mellow wall; the first bolt can be hard to spot from the ground.

Park at Lake George and hike up the climbers trail to Dike Wall, then keep walking beyond the established north face routes. Sector Mellow is the obvious slab reached first; Sector Evil Seed is a scramble up and around the right side of it. The route climbs the obvious arete.

From the north shore of Big Bear Lake, park where Greenway Drive meets Pioneer Lane and take the trails that wander up the hillside; the formations sit on the south-facing slope above. Shark Fin is west of and downhill from Big Bubba. The route takes the left arete on the north face.

Begin in the Voodoo Garden area and climb northwest along the foot of the Voodoo Garden formation. A gap opens uphill, and Shrek Rock stands there beside a big fallen tree; scramble up through large boulders to its base. The route climbs the obvious overhanging face on the south side.
